analysis.file_name: GS Malmstrom - GS Global 2027 Outlook 13 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: GS Global 2027 Outlook (Malmstrom, GS Global Banking & Markets)
key_insights: GS macro forecasts for 2027 (Peter Oppenheimer, Global Equity Strategy, '2027 Outlook: Finding Value in Growth') see a positive backdrop with equities moving higher but with high volatility.

The 2026 theme of a broadening equity bull market (more participation across regions, sectors and themes) played out despite rising oil prices and bond yields. The main driver was strong corporate earnings growth in all regions.
For 2027, profit growth and AI capex growth look poised to slow in most regions. Part of this is already priced in, with equity valuations down substantially, particularly in Tech.
Slower growth and earnings, together with moderating inflation and lower bond yields and oil prices, give a path for the equity bull market to continue.
The range of potential outcomes has widened. Given stock concentration in the US and Asia, results depend heavily on AI capex progress.
Growth is the preferred theme. As earnings slow and margins moderate, GS expects investors to reward growth companies more, especially as valuations become more attractive.

Some AI companies have de-rated sharply on anxiety about peak AI capex speed and slower returns. GS sees attractive entry points in large-capex Hyperscalers, citing strong balance sheets and diversified income streams.
GS also sees upside in more cyclical growth areas such as memory and chips.
Regional weightings: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe.
The deck names three focus areas for 2027: Growth, selective Defensives, and beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields.

Valuation charts (per captions): Value has sharply outperformed Growth in all regions, Value is no longer as cheap and Growth no longer as expensive, global Tech valuations have fallen sharply versus history and other sectors, the premium of the largest US companies has narrowed, and Cyclicals have de-rated sharply relative to Defensives.

Chart captions also state that earnings revisions have been unusually positive, MSCI ACWI P/E and PEG are around 35-year averages, earnings growth is poised to more than halve across major markets in 2027, and the earnings boost from Hyperscaler capex should fade.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations have already fallen substantially, especially in Tech. Hyperscalers have strong balance sheets and diversified income, and moderating inflation with lower yields and oil supports the bull market.
